chunk_findings.detail: The patch mirrors the `review.triaged` event to sibling gates, but it still calls `_settle_after_cap` only for the gate being triaged. Given a combined review with gates `A` and `B`, each containing the same finding digest, and a per-gate settlement cap of 1, triaging `A` as settled appends a settled triage event for `B` via `_mirror_sibling_gates`, then reloads state and computes counts only for `A`. `_settle_after_cap` is never called for `B`, so `B` does not receive its gate-level `review.settled` event even though its finding has been answered. The sibling gate therefore remains unsettled/open despite the fix’s “triage once answers both” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_settle_after_cap call

chunk_findings.detail: `_mirror_sibling_gates` only appends `review.triaged` events for the sibling gates; the settle pass is still run only for the gate that was explicitly triaged. For a combined `rubber_duck,critic` review where each gate has one triageable finding with the same digest and the gate cap is 1, triaging `rubber_duck` appends a `critic` `review.triaged` event, but after reload the code computes `counts` for `rubber_duck` and calls `_settle_after_cap(..., "rubber_duck", ...)`. No `_settle_after_cap` is run for `critic`, so `critic` can remain unsettled/open even though its only finding was just answered, leaving the agent to deal with the sibling gate again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:194

chunk_findings.detail: The mirrored `review.triaged` events are appended for the sibling gates, but after `_load` the code still calls `_settle_after_cap` only for the original `gate`. A combined review with a single finding shows the defect: triaging `rubber_duck` #1 records a verdict for `critic` via `_mirror_sibling_gates`, yet only `rubber_duck` is passed to `_settle_after_cap`, so `critic` is never settled once its triage count reaches cap. The sibling gate remains unsettled, so the same finding can still be requested again for that gate, which is the original triaged-twice bug for any gate completed by mirroring rather than an explicit triage in that gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:213

chunk_findings.detail: `_settle_recorded` appends settlement lines for mirrored sibling gates into the same `text`, and `review_triage` then computes `passed_on_refutation` from that combined text. The returned result is for the single `gate` passed to the call and returns that gate's `counts`, so the flag can become true when only a sibling gate settled on refutation. Example: a combined review has gates `A` and `B` sharing findings `X` and `Y`. Before this triage, `A` has `X` confirmed and `Y` untriaged, while `B` has `X` refuted and `Y` untriaged (possible because the bug being fixed allowed separate triage of the same finding under each gate). Triaging `A/Y` as refuted mirrors the refutation to `B`; if both gates' review budgets are spent, `_settle_after_cap` for `B` returns a line containing `ON REFUTATION`, while `A` still has a confirmed finding and is not passed on refutation. The API returns `gate=A` and `counts=A`'s counts, but `passed_on_refutation=True` because the sibling settlement line is in `text`, which can make callers or agents treat the triaged gate as passed on refutation when it is not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:222 (`passed_on_refutation="ON REFUTATION" in text`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new shared `text` dedup suppresses a stale settlement message for a mirrored sibling gate after the same stale reason has already been emitted for another gate. For a combined review with gates `A` and `B`, both gates failed, all findings refuted, and `reviewed_other_tree` returns the same non-empty reason `S` for both, `review_settle` first appends `A stays failed: S`; when it reaches `B`, `stale not in text` is false because `S` is already in `text`, so it does not append `B stays failed: S`. The returned text therefore answers only `A` and silently omits `B`’s stale outcome. The original dedup was per gate (the budget-spent path already said it for that gate); sharing `text` across mirrored gates loses the per-gate answer required for combined reviews.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review_settle.py:review_settle (stale branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The returned `review.triage` event is still for a specific `id=item, gate=gate`, but this change now computes `passed_on_refutation` by scanning the whole aggregated `text` after `_settle_recorded` has appended settlement lines for every mirrored sibling gate. Input: a combined review with gates `rubber_duck` and `critic` sharing the same finding digest, where `_settle_after_cap` returns `""` for `rubber_duck` but `"ON REFUTATION ..."` for `critic` because the per-gate `counts`/`reviewed_other_tree` differ. Triaging `rubber_duck` then returns `passed_on_refutation=True` for the `rubber_duck` gate even though that gate's own settlement text did not pass on refutation. The flag should be derived from the current gate's own `settled` line, as it was before this diff, not from the sibling lines appended to the shared text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py passed_on_refutation="ON REFUTATION" in text

chunk_findings.detail: The loop records a passed gate before evaluating later sibling gates, but it reloads state on each iteration. Given a combined review with gates A and B, both failed, all findings refuted, `settle_all_refuted` enabled, and `out.data["mirrored"] == ["B"]`, the first iteration for A calls `GD.record(..., "passed", ...)`. The next iteration loads the updated state where A is now passed, so `reviewed_other_tree(repo, cfg, st, item, "B")` sees A as the already-reviewed other tree and returns stale; B is then skipped with a stale note and is never recorded as passed. The combined triage still leaves the sibling gate to be triaged/settled, which is the bug this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review_settle.py:for g in gates loop
